title: surgical-trim-of-transitive-sdk-deps-and-stabilize-typed-client-contracts
creator: Ravi Malhotra
description: Why: Over time the SDKs accumulated a large number of transitive dependencies (quantization runtimes, legacy response shim libraries, polyfills) that inflate install size, increase CVE surface, and create brittle mismatches across Python/JS/Go bindings. Simultaneously, several legacy API surface fields (legacy_response_wrapper, old_embed_params, compat_token) remain in clients and add conditional branches across codepaths. This ticket performs a focused, low-risk cleanup: prune unused transitive deps, tighten semver ranges, introduce small compatibility adapters, and produce a clear, documented deprecation/migration path for partners.
acceptance_criteria: All SDK packages (python/js/go) have transitive dependency tree reduced by >= 20% in number of unique packages or equivalent size savings as measured by dep-tree audit
No runtime test regressions across the core integration matrix (node12/16/18, python3.9/3.10/3.11, go1.19/1.20) — validated on CI matrix
Deprecated API flags removed from public surface; compatibility adapter preserves behavior when opt-in flag legacy_mode=true is set for 90 days
New CHANGELOG entries for each client with migration notes and explicit semver implications
Two-stage rollout: canary users (10%) then full release with post-rollout monitoring showing no increase in error rates or latency for inference calls
Security scan (Snyk/OSS-Fuzz) shows no new high/critical alerts introduced by dependency changes
implementation_plan: Audit: run dep-tree and license/CVE scan across python/js/go SDKs and enumerate top 30 transitive dependencies by size and risk
Classification: mark deps as REMOVE / PIN / ISOLATE (adapter) with rationale
Python changes: pin semver ranges, replace heavy runtime polyfills with tiny shims, vendor tiny ABI adapter for older TLS stacks where unavoidable
JS changes: switch to lighter tree-shakable helpers, remove legacy response wrapper runtime and replace with small adapter module exported separately
Go changes: remove unused helper packages by inlining small utilities; tighten module requirements and run go mod tidy; add build tags for legacy behavior
Compatibility adapters: implement thin adapter layer that rehydrates legacy response shape when legacy_mode true; publish adapters as optional packages to avoid transitive bloat
CI and Benchmarks: add dep-change job to CI that measures install size and warm-start latency; run integration load tests against staging serving runtime
Rollout: publish canary SDK release to internal org, enable canary flag in Console for 10% of requests, monitor for 7 days, then promote
Docs & Migration: update SDK docs, add migration guides and code samples for common breaking changes
migration_notes: We will not immediately remove behavior. First release introduces adapter and logs deprecation warnings. After 90 days and no significant fallout, next minor release will remove deprecated flags and actually drop heavy transitive deps from the default install. Enterprise customers on Private will be offered a backport patch if required.
testing_plan: Unit + integration test updates for all removed/shimmed modules
End-to-end smoke tests against hosted API and dedicated stacks with pinned model variants
Performance regression suite: token-generation latency P95/P99, cold-start CPU/GPU overhead
Canary traffic harness with synthetic prompts and customer-like prompt mix
Dependency-failure simulation: force transitive absence and validate adapter fallback paths
risks: Unexpected subtle behavioral diffs from removed helper libs leading to downstream SDK consumers seeing changed serialization/edge-case behavior
Transient CI flakes due to tighter versions exposing flaky tests; mitigated with quarantined flaky suites
Enterprise customers pinned to older transitive dep versions might experience installation conflicts — mitigation: backport adapters and offer pinned-compat releases
Size/publish pipeline regressions for languages with larger packaging surfaces (python wheels, npm bundles)
Build time increases while vendoring or creating adapters
